page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard3.64 is a bare metal compute instance powered by two Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processors (x86_64 architecture). It provides 64 physical cores (128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled) operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, accompanied by 48 MB of L3 cache. The platform is configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core (or 8.0 GB per vCPU in a 1:8 configuration). The system does not include local disk storage or discrete GPUs, requiring remote block or object storage for persistent data, and includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput in parallel workloads and memory-intensive operations. Multi-core performance measured via stress-ng reached 116,299.16, placing the instance in the top 25% tier, supported by 482.21 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by an uncached read bandwidth of 338.31 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 135.72 GB/sec. This memory architecture translates into high transactional efficiency, recording 103.89 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and top-tier static web serving throughput of 153.97 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing presents a tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the average tier and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the lower quartile.

Instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI) alongside standard vector and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. These features assist in CPU-bound machine learning tasks, with prompt processing on a medium 7B model reaching 182.1 tokens per second. Cost efficiency derives from high physical core density and substantial memory capacity in a non-virtualized bare metal setup, avoiding virtualization overhead. BM.Standard3.64 is well suited for memory-intensive in-memory data grids, large enterprise databases, multi-threaded batch processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard3.64 is a bare metal server featuring 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs on Intel Xeon 8358 processors (x86_64) running at 2.6 GHz. Equipped with 1024 GB of DDR4 RAM, the platform offers significant memory density without integrated local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluation shows upper-quartile multi-core processing in stress-ng (116,299.16) and uncached memory read bandwidth of 338.31 GB/sec. It demonstrates top-tier web serving throughput of 153.97 GB/sec and handles over 103 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread operations reflect mid-range performance, the architecture delivers high resource consolidation and parallel throughput. These hardware characteristics align directly with large in-memory databases, dense virtualization clusters, and high-volume batch data pipelines.
